name: A plague and a scapegoat
about: Sickness or famine hits a real town. Its people blame one of their own, often a hedge witch, a midwife or a beggar. The lord burns them, protects them or loses the town's love, and the sickness shows whether the fire did any good.
title: The Pestilence of {town}

name: {first} of the Fen
Old {first}
{first} the Herbwife
create.memory: I've healed the sick of {town} with herbs for thirty years. They used to thank me.

fade: The sickness hangs on in {town} for a while, and then it's just one more grief among many.

beats.speaker: lord
text: Sickness comes to {town}. It starts in the tanners' street, then reaches the market. The death carts go out at night.
In {town} the bread runs out and the coughing starts. The sept bell rings for the dead three times before noon.

memory.lord: The sickness came to {town}, and the people are looking to me.

beats.speaker: scapegoat
beats.text: In the alehouses of {town} they say {scapegoat} brought the sickness. Someone has chalked a mark on {scapegoat.his} door.

memory.scapegoat: They chalked a mark on my door in {town}. They say I brought the sickness.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} has {scapegoat} dragged in chains before the people of {town} to answer for the dead.

memory.scapegoat: {lord} put me in chains in front of the people of {town}.

beats.text: {scapegoat} is burned in the square at {town}. The crowd that screamed for it goes home quiet.

memory.lord: I burned {scapegoat} in the square at {town} to calm the people.

die.how: They burned me in {town} for a sickness I didn't bring.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: The burning changed nothing. People in {town} keep dying, and now they whisper that {lord} burned the wrong {scapegoat.man}.

memory.lord: I burned {scapegoat}, but people kept dying. The people of {town} look at me differently now.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: The sickness finally leaves {town}. {lord} has the ashes thrown in the river and calls it justice, and nobody argues with {lord.him}.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} stands at {scapegoat}'s door with a drawn sword and says the first man to touch it will hang.

memory.scapegoat: {lord} stood at my door with a sword when all of {town} wanted me dead.
memory.lord: I stood between the people of {town} and {scapegoat}.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} finds no proof against {scapegoat} and lets {scapegoat.him} go. The crowd outside doesn't agree.
The hungry of {town} riot. They break into {lord}'s granary and come for {scapegoat} with torches.

memory.lord: The people of {town} broke into my granary and hunted {scapegoat} through the streets.

die.how: The mob in {town} dragged me out of my house.

beats.text: By morning {scapegoat} has fled {town} over the wall with whatever {scapegoat.he} could carry. The sickness stays a while longer, and then it goes too.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {scapegoat} is dead, killed by the people {scapegoat.he} lived among in {town}. {lord} hangs two of them, but it changes nothing.

memory.lord: The people of {town} murdered {scapegoat} and I couldn't stop them.

beats.text: The sickness burns itself out. Nobody in {town} mentions {scapegoat} again, and people bless {lord}'s name in the septs.
The sickness takes {lord} {lord.himself}. In {town} they say it's a judgment, but they don't say for what.
